title: Comprehensive Grammar Examination
orientation:
This examination brings together the structures studied throughout the course. It samples recognition, explanation, contextual application, sentence revision and independent writing. Work from the meaning and conditions stated in each question; some sentences are deliberately correct despite looking unusual. Attempt the objective items and write your responses before opening feedback. You may use more than one study session, but record whether you consulted a reference so that you can interpret the result honestly.

The report should guide a specific revision plan. It is not an official past paper, a calibrated proficiency test or a promise of an examination mark. Keep first responses distinct from later retries, and compare written responses with their criteria rather than matching the model word for word. A high recognition score can coexist with weaknesses in extended writing. Day 30 will provide another integrated sample and a continuing development plan.
outcomes: Analyse grammatical categories and functions inside unfamiliar sentences.
Select defensible forms in explicit contexts and recognise genuine no-error cases.
Transform and edit while retaining tense, scope, participants and modality.
Produce connected formal writing with clear reference and qualified claims.
Use the concept-level report to choose a fresh revision activity.

modules.title: Recognise the structure, then justify the interpretation
modules.definition: An integrated grammar assessment samples several related abilities: recognising a form, explaining its meaning, applying it in context and revising or producing language. A selected answer supplies evidence about the item attempted, not every possible use of its grammatical topic.
foundation: Begin with the whole message before inspecting its parts. In The files that the auditor requested have arrived, the subject is a noun phrase headed by files; the relative clause adds information inside that phrase. Have agrees with files, while requested belongs to the embedded clause. Naming only the nearest noun would miss the structure. For each objective item, identify what its wording asks: a word class, a grammatical function, a suitable form or a justified interpretation. These are different questions, even when they use the same example sentence.
intermediate: A contextual gap asks which form fits the situation stated, not which form you have memorised after a particular signal word. Since can introduce a starting point or a reason; by can locate a deadline without mechanically requiring a future perfect. Read the supplied interpretation and surrounding clauses. Where an item asks for an error, keep a genuine no-error possibility available. A familiar-looking construction may be standard in a specified variety or register. Conversely, understanding the intended message does not make every word form or clause boundary acceptable in edited prose.
advanced: A difficult analysis may require more than one level. In Whether the committee recommended closure remains unclear, the initial interrogative clause functions as subject of remains. The order inside it is not direct-question inversion. The content of that clause can still be analysed into its own subject, verb and object relationship. Separate this hierarchical analysis from stylistic preference. A shorter paraphrase might be easier for a particular audience, but that does not establish a grammatical defect in the original. An answer explanation should identify the relevant relationship and show why competing interpretations fail in the stated context.
expert: Treat an objective key as a claim that must survive scrutiny. If two options appear defensible, state their readings and compare them with the question’s explicit conditions; do not invent an examiner’s preference. Some grammatical differences are genuine alternatives, while others become equivalent only after a meaning change. This assessment uses a British editorial default and identifies established alternatives where they matter. Its difficulty labels describe the intended depth of reasoning, not calibrated psychometric levels. When you self-review an unfamiliar analysis, distinguish a mistaken label from a faulty interpretation and from an unsupported rule; the revision action should address the actual gap.

patterns.meaning: Three related questions that should not be collapsed into one label.
Use all three when justifying a gap answer.

examples.analysis: Minutes is a plural noun here and the whole noun phrase is the subject of a passive clause.

examples.sentence: The minutes that Salma revised were circulated.
examples.analysis: The subject contains a relative clause; revised does not control the main-clause agreement.

examples.sentence: Whether the revised minutes were circulated remains uncertain.
examples.analysis: The initial interrogative clause functions as subject of remains; its own subject is the revised minutes.

contrasts.b: I wonder which minutes were circulated.
contrasts.note: Both grammatical. The first is a direct interrogative; in this particular pair which minutes is the subject in both clauses, so there is no additional do-support inversion.

exceptions: An indirect question need not contain a visually different order from its corresponding subject question: who arrived remains who arrived. Analyse function rather than demanding a mechanical word swap.

mistakes.problem: The nearest noun before a verb must control its number.
mistakes.repair: Identify the grammatical subject and the head or construction that determines agreement.
mistakes.reason: Intervening modifiers and embedded clauses can contain other nouns.

mistakes.problem: Every unfamiliar construction should be corrected.
mistakes.repair: Name a defensible grammatical problem before changing a construction.
mistakes.reason: A standard alternative, regional convention or marked but licensed structure may require no correction.

glossary.definition: An assessment sampling several abilities and topic areas together.
glossary.example: Recognition, editing and original writing occur in the same examination.

glossary.definition: Analysis of a grammatical unit inside a larger unit.
glossary.example: A relative clause inside a subject noun phrase.

modules.title: Transform, edit and write without distorting the message
modules.definition: A meaning-preserving transformation changes a requested structure while retaining the relevant participants, time, modality, quantity and logical relationships. Editing also requires deciding which changes are necessary and which are optional improvements for the specified audience.
foundation: Write a small meaning ledger before a substantial revision. Record who did what, when it happened, how certain the statement is and which conditions or limits apply. The council may extend some routes if funding continues is not equivalent to The council will extend all routes. The second version changes possibility, quantity and condition at once. When transforming an active clause into a passive, preserve the tense and aspect rather than copying only a participle: has approved becomes has been approved, with agreement adjusted to the new subject. Include the agent where the task requires that information.
intermediate: An open correction can have several defensible solutions. The report arrived late, the review continued can become two sentences, a semicolon-linked sentence or an appropriately coordinated sentence. The choice should preserve the intended relationship. Adding therefore would assert a result relationship that the original did not supply. A model solution is one worked demonstration, while a rubric lists the features that a different answer must satisfy. Use the rubric to compare your response, and explain legitimate alternatives rather than attempting to match every word of the model.
advanced: Paragraph editing adds reference and information flow to sentence-level accuracy. Resolve an ambiguous pronoun by identifying its intended referent before replacing it; do not decide who acted merely because one reading is easier to rewrite. Check that reduced clauses retain their intended subjects, comparisons compare comparable things, and connectors describe the relationship supported by the passage. Quotation and capitalisation conventions can reflect house style, so a consistent alternative may be acceptable. In formal original writing, make grammar serve the explanation: a clear short clause may communicate better than an unnecessary cleft, inversion or nominalisation.
expert: Transformation is not a promise of complete synonymy. Active and passive versions can organise information differently, and a cleft can introduce focus or a presupposed background. A grammatical transformation may therefore preserve core event content while altering discourse effect. State that limitation when relevant. The assessment asks for particular invariants so that a response can be judged fairly. If the proposed change cannot preserve them, explain the restriction rather than forcing a superficially similar sentence. Independent production must also be reviewed for appropriate commitments and coherent argument; an accurate collection of isolated forms is not automatically a successful paragraph.

patterns.form: original meaning ledger → requested form → invariant check
patterns.meaning: A practical method for preserving important content.
Check time, subject interpretation and information loss before accepting compression.

examples.sentence: The panel has accepted the revised timetable.
examples.analysis: Its present-perfect passive is The revised timetable has been accepted by the panel.

examples.sentence: Some evening sessions may be cancelled if demand remains low.
examples.analysis: A summary must retain limited quantity, possibility and the condition.

examples.sentence: After Naila inspected the valve, the leak was repaired.
examples.analysis: The finite after-clause explicitly identifies the inspector; the passive main clause need not share that subject.

contrasts.a: The bridge closed, so the school trip was postponed.
contrasts.b: The bridge closed; the school trip was postponed.
contrasts.note: Both grammatical, but only the first explicitly asserts a result relationship. Do not substitute it when that relationship has not been supplied.

exceptions: A passive main clause is compatible with an introductory finite clause having its own subject, as in After the engineer arrived, the test was repeated. Passivity alone does not create a dangling modifier.

mistakes.problem: Compress Some may benefit into All will benefit.
mistakes.repair: Retain Some may benefit when quantity and uncertainty are essential.
mistakes.reason: Concision cannot justify reversing the scope or strength of a claim.

mistakes.problem: Use a model answer as the only permitted wording.
mistakes.repair: Accept another grammatical response that fulfils the stated invariants and rubric.
mistakes.reason: Open production permits alternatives that an exact-string comparison would reject.

glossary.definition: A record of content that a revision must preserve.
glossary.example: two clinics; possible extension; only if funding continues

glossary.definition: A specified feature that must remain constant during a transformation.
glossary.example: The action remains present perfect in the passive version.

modules.title: Read the evidence report and choose a precise revision action
modules.definition: A topic-level performance report organises evidence by the underlying grammatical concepts and abilities sampled. Completion, first-response accuracy, repeated-item retrieval and writing self-review are separate records and support different conclusions.
foundation: After attempting the examination, list the concepts behind errors before deciding what to reread. A score of twenty correct answers does not reveal whether the remaining difficulties concern reference, tense or punctuation. Link each error to its explanation and lesson, then state the distinction in your own words. Record a written task as attempted when you have produced a response; record its self-review separately after comparing it with the rubric. A model reveal is useful feedback, but it cannot establish that your original response was independently accurate.
intermediate: Keep first responses separate from later retries. An answer selected after reading the explanation is evidence of a learning activity, not another unfamiliar item. A later spaced success may show retention of that particular distinction, especially when you can explain why it works. However, repeated recognition does not establish control in original writing. For an agreement weakness, combine a fresh subject analysis, a correction task and an original sentence. For a cohesion weakness, review an extended passage rather than relying only on a single-gap item about a connector.
advanced: Compare ability profiles as well as topic labels. A learner may identify a passive correctly but change its tense while transforming a sentence, or choose the correct article in a gap while omitting it in a paragraph. These are different application demands. Look at the size and variety of the evidence before making a broad claim: one difficult error is not proof of failure across an entire domain, and one easy success is not mastery. Difficulty labels are instructional judgements. The course does not claim that the labels or raw counts convert directly into official examination marks, university grades or CEFR levels.
expert: A defensible report includes limits. The bank samples selected forms and interpretations; it cannot exhaust every lexical restriction, dialect or writing situation. Self-reviewed open responses depend on the learner’s judgement, while objective keys assume the context stated in each item. Use the report to set an observable next action: revise the countability contrast, explain two new examples and attempt a different short response before a scheduled retrieval. Retain the original error record so that improvement is not confused with rewriting the baseline. Continuing evaluation should gradually include unfamiliar language and independent written expression, not merely higher scores on remembered questions.

patterns.form: error → concept → different application → later retrieval
patterns.meaning: Links feedback to a specific revision action.

patterns.form: first responses + repeated retrieval + written production
patterns.meaning: Separate evidence streams that should not be collapsed into one artificial mastery mark.

examples.sentence: First attempt: four of six agreement items correct.
examples.analysis: This describes the sampled items; it does not certify agreement mastery.

examples.sentence: A repeated item was answered correctly after its explanation.
examples.analysis: That response is useful practice, but is not a new independent question.

examples.sentence: A learner identifies a dangling opening and then writes three clear finite-clause alternatives.
examples.analysis: Analysis and production supply complementary evidence about a practical correction skill.

contrasts.note: The first can be a completion statement; the second requires much stronger evidence and is not inferred here.

exceptions: A single unusual but legitimate construction should not become an error simply because it conflicts with an oversimplified remembered rule. Recheck context, region and register before revising the report.

mistakes.problem: I revealed the writing model, so my paragraph earns full marks.
mistakes.repair: I revealed the model and must compare my own paragraph with its rubric.
mistakes.reason: Revealing content is not an objective evaluation of an original response.

mistakes.problem: I answered the same item five times, so I have five independent successes.
mistakes.repair: I have five responses to one exposed item, with the first response and later retrieval distinguished.
mistakes.reason: Exposure changes what the repeated response can establish.

glossary.definition: The learner’s earliest recorded answer to an item in the relevant record.
glossary.example: A later retry does not replace the initial selected answer.

glossary.definition: Evidence grouped by the grammatical concept actually sampled.
glossary.example: Article selection and countability receive separate revision actions.

questions.prompt: In a glass roof, which analysis separates category from function?
options: Glass is a noun functioning as a modifier of roof.
Glass is an adverb because it describes something.
Roof is necessarily the subject wherever the phrase appears.
questions.why: Glass retains noun category while functioning as a premodifier; the phrase’s external function depends on its sentence context.

questions.prompt: In the transparent structure care + -less + -ness, what does -ness do?
options: Forms a noun from the adjective careless
questions.why: -ness is derivational here: careless is an adjective and carelessness is a noun. It does not mark plural, tense or comparison.

questions.prompt: Complete the standard negative: The camera does not ____ the entrance.
questions.why: Do-support carries present tense and agreement; the following lexical verb takes its plain form record.

questions.prompt: The catalogue lists six individual ____ of furniture.
questions.why: Items supplies a countable unit for ordinary uncountable furniture. The intended structure is six individual items of furniture.

questions.prompt: Introduce an unidentified period of sixty minutes: We waited for ____ hour before the gates opened.
questions.why: Hour begins with a vowel sound, so indefinite an is appropriate. The other choices do not fit this singular noun phrase.

questions.prompt: Which sentence presents a small but available quantity of time positively?
options: We have little time, so time is abundant.
We have a few time for a check.
We have many time for a check.
We have a little time, so we can check the figures.
questions.why: A little can present a small useful amount. Little tends to emphasise scarcity; a few and many do not quantify uncountable time in this sense.

questions.prompt: An applicant’s gender is unspecified: Each applicant should bring their own identification. Which judgement is defensible?
options: Each applicant must be changed to all applicants.
The sentence uses established singular-they reference.
Their must be followed by identification are.
questions.why: Singular their can refer to the unspecified person introduced by each applicant. The noun phrase remains singular where its own agreement requires it.

questions.prompt: The invitation was addressed to Fatima and ____.
questions.why: Objective me fits the coordinated complement of to. The simple case relationship is visible in addressed to me; reflexive myself is not required here.

questions.prompt: The alarm ____ at seven yesterday, and the building was empty by eight.
questions.why: The completed event is located in the finished past by yesterday. Past simple sounded fits that narrative context.

questions.prompt: Choose the wording that explicitly states continuing activity up to now.
options: The team will sort the files next month.
The team has been sorting the files since nine and is still doing so.
The team sorted the files yesterday and then left.
The team had sorted the files before the inspection began.
questions.why: The perfect progressive links the activity to now, and is still doing so explicitly confirms continuation. The other options locate the event elsewhere.

questions.prompt: Use the future-perfect form to present completion before next Friday: By next Friday, the crew ____ the roof.
questions.why: Future-perfect will have repaired presents the repair as complete by the future reference point. The prompt specifically requests this form; by alone would not force it in every context.

questions.prompt: The standard of the shortlisted essays ____ improved.
questions.why: The singular head standard controls the main verb; essays is inside an of-phrase. Has improved is the appropriate singular perfect form.

questions.prompt: Which comparison explicitly compares running costs with running costs?
options: Our running costs are lower than expensive buildings.
Our running costs are lower than the other building is large.
Our running costs are lower than the other building.
Our running costs are lower than those of the other building.
questions.why: Those of the other building stands for its running costs, making the compared categories parallel.

questions.prompt: Which sentence explicitly restricts the subject to Nadia and excludes other people from knowing the access code?
options: Only Nadia knows the access code.
Nadia knows only the access code.
Nadia knows the access code only on Mondays.
Nadia almost knows the access code.
questions.why: Only Nadia focuses the subject under the intended exclusion. The other positions or adverbs restrict the object, time or degree instead.

questions.prompt: The editor insists ____ the source before publication. Choose the standard pattern with an -ing complement.
questions.why: Insist on selects a noun phrase or an -ing clause here: insists on checking the source. Insist that the source be checked is another standard pattern, but requires a finite clause.

questions.prompt: What is the head of the phrase the unusually broad avenue beside the station?
questions.why: Avenue heads the whole noun phrase. Station heads the smaller noun phrase inside the postmodifying prepositional phrase.

questions.prompt: Using the traditional finite-clause classification, choose the complex sentence.
options: The guard and the visitor waited outside.
The guard nodded; the visitor entered.
The guard nodded and opened the door.
The guard nodded because the visitor had identified herself.
questions.why: The guard nodded because the visitor had identified herself contains a main clause plus a finite subordinate reason clause. The option with two people waiting has one clause; nodded and opened shares one subject with coordinated verb phrases; the semicolon version coordinates two main clauses.

questions.prompt: Which relative construction leaves the appropriate object gap?
options: The painting whom we borrowed is insured.
The painting which we borrowed it is insured.
The painting that we borrowed is insured.
The painting that we borrowed it is insured.
questions.why: The relative marker corresponds to the object of borrowed, so no resumptive it is added in this standard edited construction. Whom is not appropriate for the non-person painting.

questions.prompt: Choose a valid boundary before connective however.
options: The test; ended however the review continued.
The test ended, however, the review continued.
The test ended; however, the review continued.
The test ended however; the review continued.
questions.why: The semicolon separates the two main clauses, and a comma follows the introductory connective adverb. However does not by itself license a comma splice.

questions.prompt: The reservation was made, but it was unnecessary: You ____ a table; several were empty.
options: must not have reserved, meaning a known completed action
questions.why: Needn’t have reserved normally presents a completed reservation as unnecessary. The context explicitly supplies both completion and absence of necessity.

questions.prompt: The speaker imagines a different past cause and present consequence: If I had accepted that job, I ____ in Leeds now.
questions.why: The past-perfect condition concerns a counterfactual past decision; would be living gives the imagined present consequence, a mixed-time conditional.

questions.prompt: Make They might have removed the warning passive while preserving its modal-perfect meaning.
options: The warning might have being removed.
The warning might have been removed.
The warning might has been removed.
questions.why: Might + have + been + removed preserves modal possibility and perfect anteriority in a passive verb phrase.

questions.prompt: The driver paused the journey in order to check the map: The driver stopped ____.
options: checking the map, meaning ended that activity
questions.why: Stopped to check uses the infinitive to express purpose. Stopped checking would normally mean ending the checking activity, contrary to the stated meaning.

questions.prompt: Identify an error in By whom the painting was restored remains unknown.
options: By whom must be replaced with by who.
was restored must be changed to restored was.
questions.why: The initial embedded interrogative functions as the subject of remains. Its internal statement order is appropriate; by whom is a formal prepositional interrogative phrase.

questions.prompt: Mira is the intended inspector. Which opening explicitly preserves that subject?
options: After inspecting the cable, the damage alarmed Mira.
After Mira inspected the cable, the damage alarmed her.
Having inspected the cable, the damage was alarming.
To inspect the cable, the damage appeared serious.
questions.why: The finite after-clause names Mira as the inspector, while the main clause states her reaction. The other openings make the subject interpretation faulty for the intended meaning.

questions.prompt: Front Only after the inspection in We opened the vault only after the inspection.
options: Only after the inspection did we opened the vault.
Only after the inspection opened we did the vault.
Only after the inspection we opened the vault.
Only after the inspection did we open the vault.
questions.why: The fronted restrictive adverbial triggers subject–auxiliary inversion; do-support supplies did and the lexical verb becomes plain open.

questions.prompt: Several nurses have separate lockers. Which plural possessive fits?
options: the nurse’s lockers, necessarily meaning several nurses
questions.why: The regular plural nurses ends in s, so its possessive is nurses’. Nurse’s would ordinarily identify one nurse, not the specified several.

questions.prompt: In British English with the committee members viewed collectively, identify an error in The committee have reached their decision.
options: have must be has in every variety and context.
their must be its in every variety and context.
questions.why: Plural collective agreement and plural-member reference are established in British English. Singular unit agreement would also be possible with a compatible interpretation; it is not a compulsory correction here.

questions.prompt: Analyse The board appointed Amira chair: identify the subject, object and object complement.
questions.model: The board is the subject; Amira is the direct object; chair is a noun functioning as object complement and describing the role assigned to Amira.
rubric: Identify whole phrases rather than just their heads.
Distinguish the object from the complement predicated of that object.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Use ordinary general senses and keep the stated quantities: We received two ____ of advice and three ____ of equipment. Supply appropriate countable unit nouns.
questions.model: We received two pieces of advice and three items of equipment.
rubric: Keep advice and equipment uninflected in their ordinary general senses.
Use countable unit nouns that fit two and three.
alternatives: Pieces can also be used for equipment; other suitable unit nouns are acceptable where their meanings fit.

questions.prompt: Explain the normal reference difference between A visitor is waiting and The visitor is waiting.
questions.model: A visitor introduces an indefinite visitor without presenting that person as already identifiable; the visitor presents the referent as identifiable in the current context. Neither article alone specifies whether the speaker knows the person’s identity.
rubric: Discuss identifiability to the addressee, not merely physical uniqueness.
Do not equate indefinite reference with necessarily unknown identity.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: The person who left the bag is unidentified. Explain why Someone has left their bag does not require his or her in contemporary standard English.
questions.model: Someone takes singular has in its clause; singular their is an established possessive form referring to an unspecified person. His or her is possible in suitable contexts but is not grammatically required.
rubric: Separate the agreement of someone from the pronoun paradigm used later.
Recognise singular they without making a claim about the unidentified person’s gender.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: The file was missing when I arrived at noon. Supply an appropriate perfect form of disappear to show anteriority: By noon, the file ____.
questions.model: By noon, the file had disappeared.
rubric: Use had + past participle to look back from the stated past reference point.
Do not add a passive auxiliary to intransitive disappear.
alternatives: A fuller answer such as had already disappeared is acceptable.

questions.prompt: Explain why will is legitimate in If you will wait by the entrance, I will fetch the guide, with a willingness interpretation.
questions.model: Will in the conditional clause can express willingness: if you are willing to wait. It is therefore not merely a mechanical future marker forbidden after every if. The main clause states the offered future action.
rubric: Identify the intended modal meaning of will.
Reject an indiscriminate ban on will in all if-clauses.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Classify hard and hardly in He worked hard but hardly spoke, and explain their meanings.
questions.model: Both are adverbs here. Hard means with effort; hardly means scarcely or almost not. Their meanings are not interchangeable.
rubric: Identify the class from the constructions.
Explain the semantic contrast rather than treating -ly as a harmless spelling change.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Arrange all supplied tokens into one ordinary imperative: it / please / off / switch. Do not add words.
rubric: Use every supplied token once.
Place the unstressed pronoun object between switch and off.
alternatives: Switch it off, please.

questions.prompt: Give two plausible attachments for beside the museum in I photographed the visitor beside the museum. State whether the phrase can locate the photographing event or describe the visitor.
questions.model: It can locate the event: Beside the museum, I photographed the visitor. It can modify the visitor: I photographed the visitor who was beside the museum. Context is needed to select the intended attachment.
rubric: Supply two distinct attachment analyses.
Do not invent additional facts to insist that only one reading is possible.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Combine these statements using a supplementary relative clause without deleting either fact: The manuscript was damaged. It was recovered from the cellar.
questions.model: The manuscript, which was recovered from the cellar, was damaged.
rubric: Preserve both the damage and the recovery facts.
Use commas to mark the supplementary relative and avoid a repeated object/subject pronoun inside it.
alternatives: The manuscript, which was damaged, was recovered from the cellar.

questions.prompt: Split the following into two complete written sentences without adding a result or reason claim: The survey ended in April, and the findings were published in June.
questions.model: The survey ended in April. The findings were published in June.
rubric: Retain the two dates and events.
Supply complete clauses and correct sentence-final punctuation.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Contrast She needn’t have travelled and She didn’t need to travel. Explain what can be inferred about the journey.
questions.model: Needn’t have travelled normally presents an actual journey as unnecessary. Didn’t need to travel states absence of necessity; whether she travelled depends on context rather than the form alone.
rubric: Distinguish an unnecessary completed action from a statement of no necessity.
Do not claim that didn’t need to invariably proves non-performance.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Identify the time relationship in If the council had approved the grant, the centre would be open now.
questions.model: The if-clause imagines a different past approval; the main clause imagines a present consequence. It is a counterfactual mixed-time conditional, not a description of an actual approval.
rubric: Identify the past condition and present result separately.
Explain the remote/counterfactual interpretation without treating numbered labels as the only possible grammar.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: Edit genuine grammatical and boundary errors only: The old map were difficult to read. It contained several informations about wells, however, the surveyors needed a newer source.
questions.model: The old map was difficult to read. It contained several pieces of information about wells; however, the surveyors needed a newer source.
rubric: Repair singular map/was agreement.
Use an appropriate countable unit for information.
Repair the main-clause boundary before however while preserving the contrast.
alternatives: A full stop before However is also valid.

questions.prompt: Focus the location with an it-cleft: The team found the ledger in the attic. Preserve the past event and all participants.
questions.model: It was in the attic that the team found the ledger.
rubric: Use past was in the cleft frame.
Preserve the team as finder and the ledger as object.
Recognise that focus changes even though the core event content is retained.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

questions.prompt: A learner answers six distinct items correctly, then repeats one of those items four times after reading its explanation. State a defensible evidence report and one next revision action.
questions.model: Six distinct items were answered correctly; one of them received four additional exposed responses. The extra responses are practice on one item, not four new independent successes. Next, attempt an unfamiliar response task on the same underlying concept and explain the choice.
rubric: Keep the number of distinct items at six.
Label exposure and retries separately.
Recommend an observable new application rather than declare full topic mastery.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Correct genuine errors: The condition of the storage rooms have deteriorated.
corrections.model: The condition of the storage rooms has deteriorated.
rubric: Identify singular condition as the subject head.
Preserve present-perfect meaning while correcting agreement.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Correct the article: A auditor inspected the original accounts.
corrections.model: An auditor inspected the original accounts.
rubric: Choose the article by the initial vowel sound in auditor.
Retain the person and completed inspection event.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: The guide is intended to have read the notice. Repair Having read the notice, the visitors were warned by the guide.
corrections.model: After the guide had read the notice, the visitors were warned by the guide.
rubric: Make the guide the explicit reader.
Retain the visitors as recipients of the warning.
alternatives: Having read the notice, the guide warned the visitors.

corrections.prompt: Correct an ordinary indirect question: The curator asked where had the painting been stored.
corrections.model: The curator asked where the painting had been stored.
rubric: Use subject-before-auxiliary order inside the embedded question.
Preserve past-perfect passive meaning.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

corrections.prompt: Correct the connector pattern: The inspection stopped because of the room was unsafe.
corrections.model: The inspection stopped because the room was unsafe.
rubric: Use because before a finite reason clause.
Do not remove the reason or replace it with a result.
alternatives: The inspection stopped because of the unsafe room.

corrections.prompt: Repair the comparison without changing the intended comparison of two salaries: Her salary is higher than her assistant.
corrections.model: Her salary is higher than her assistant’s.
rubric: Compare salary with salary.
Retain the direction of the comparison.
alternatives: Her salary is higher than that of her assistant.

corrections.prompt: Repair the boundary: The hearing resumed, nevertheless, the main witness was absent.
corrections.model: The hearing resumed; nevertheless, the main witness was absent.
rubric: Use a valid boundary between main clauses.
Retain the concessive relationship.
alternatives: The hearing resumed. Nevertheless, the main witness was absent.

corrections.prompt: In British English, with the members considered individually, correct only genuine errors: The committee are divided in their opinions.
corrections.model: No change is required: The committee are divided in their opinions.
rubric: Recognise established British plural collective agreement.
Do not force singular agreement while retaining an individual-member interpretation.
alternatives: The committee members are divided in their opinions is an explicit paraphrase, not a necessary correction.

corrections.prompt: Correct only genuine errors in ordinary standard English: The colleague who I spoke to has replied.
corrections.model: No change is required: The colleague who I spoke to has replied.
rubric: Recognise object who as an established relative choice.
Recognise standard preposition stranding.
alternatives: The colleague to whom I spoke has replied is a more formal alternative.

corrections.prompt: The journey happened unnecessarily. Correct only genuine errors: We needn’t have taken a taxi.
corrections.model: No change is required: We needn’t have taken a taxi.
rubric: Retain the completed unnecessary-action meaning.
Do not add to after modal needn’t.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

transformations.prompt: Make passive and retain the agent: The conservator has repaired the damaged frame.
transformations.model: The damaged frame has been repaired by the conservator.
rubric: Preserve present perfect.
Retain both participants and singular agreement.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

transformations.prompt: At the end of Monday, report this question asked that morning using a past reporting frame: The visitor asked the porter, Did you lock the side door?
transformations.model: The visitor asked the porter whether the porter had locked the side door.
rubric: Use an embedded yes/no question with statement order.
Keep the porter as the person asked about locking.
Use a form compatible with the stated later Monday perspective.
alternatives: The visitor asked the porter if the porter had locked the side door. A clear pronoun may replace the repeated role where its reference is unambiguous.

transformations.prompt: Begin with Never and preserve tense: We had never encountered such a precise description.
transformations.model: Never had we encountered such a precise description.
rubric: Invert auxiliary had and subject we.
Retain the perfect participle encountered.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

transformations.prompt: Replace the finite purpose clause with an infinitival purpose clause and preserve its understood subject: Priya used a torch so that she could read the faded label.
transformations.model: Priya used a torch to read the faded label.
rubric: Keep Priya as the understood reader.
Retain the torch and faded-label information.
alternatives: Priya used a torch in order to read the faded label.

writing.prompt:
Complete BOTH tasks. 1. Edit the passage below for grammar only; keep all facts, quantities, uncertainty and conditions. Then state whether a grammatical change was necessary. 2. Write a160–190-word proposal about the clinic’s next step, using the supplied facts. Include a condition, a cautious claim, a passive and a coherent reference chain.

The clinic opened an evening service in May. Its first review recorded 240 visits over four weeks, but the register did not show how many different patients attended. Some patients said the later hours helped them after work. Staff said that demand might fall during the winter, when transport is less reliable. The service therefore needs a longer trial before the managers decide whether to continue it. Any expansion will depend on funding and on enough nurses volunteering for evening shifts.
writing.model:
1. No grammatical correction is necessary. Edited passage (unchanged):
The clinic opened an evening service in May. Its first review recorded 240 visits over four weeks, but the register did not show how many different patients attended. Some patients said the later hours helped them after work. Staff said that demand might fall during the winter, when transport is less reliable. The service therefore needs a longer trial before the managers decide whether to continue it. Any expansion will depend on funding and on enough nurses volunteering for evening shifts.

2. One proposal (170 words):
The clinic could continue its evening service for another three months if sufficient staff volunteer for the shifts. Its first review recorded 240 visits, but that figure does not tell us how many different patients attended. The managers should therefore collect both visit totals and patient numbers during the extended trial. They should also ask whether the later appointments help people who cannot attend during normal working hours.

Transport may become less reliable in winter, so the trial should include a record of missed appointments and the reasons patients give for them. An extension would not guarantee that demand will remain high. However, it would allow the clinic to compare different periods before making a permanent decision. The additional shifts should be funded separately, and no existing daytime service should be reduced without another review. If the findings show sustained demand and manageable costs, the managers could consider a longer arrangement. This proposal treats the first figures as useful initial evidence rather than proof that every patient needs evening appointments.

Annotation: if sufficient staff volunteer supplies a condition; may become marks possibility; should be funded is passive; the clinic/its/the managers/they form recoverable reference chains.
rubric: Task 1: preserve all facts and recognise that an already grammatical passage can be retained.
Task 2: produce 160–190 words, distinguish visits from different patients, and retain uncertainty about winter demand.
Include a condition, an appropriate passive and a cautious claim without inventing evidence.
Check reference, clause boundaries and temporal relationships; describe the result as self-review.
alternatives: Other proposals may recommend a different next step if they use the supplied evidence accurately, preserve its qualifications and meet the stated grammatical requirements.

recall.prompt: Without looking back, contrast few and a few in two original sentences about available seats.
recall.model: Few seats remained, so several visitors had to stand. / A few seats remained, so we could accommodate two more visitors.
rubric: Use plural countable seats.
Make the scarcity versus small-positive-quantity distinction explicit.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

recall.prompt: Explain why The parcel arrived cannot be converted mechanically into The parcel was arrived in ordinary standard English.
recall.model: Arrive is ordinarily intransitive in this sense and does not license that be-passive. A different verb such as deliver would describe a related event with a different argument structure, not simply passivise arrive.
rubric: Identify the valency restriction.
Do not present a lexical replacement as an exact voice transformation.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

recall.prompt: Record one weak concept from this examination, the exact distinction to review and a fresh task for tomorrow. If no error was recorded, identify one written response that still merits checking.
recall.model: Revision note: I confused a recipient object with an object complement. Tomorrow I will analyse three new verb patterns and explain whether the final phrase receives something or is predicated of the object. I will compare my analysis with the worked models before attempting later retrieval.
rubric: Name a precise concept and distinction.
Set an observable fresh application, not just reread grammar.
Keep written self-review separate from an objective mark.
alternatives: A different formulation is valid if it preserves the stated meaning and fulfils the specific structural requirements.

I wrote corrections and transformations before comparing models.
I checked written responses against meaning and structural criteria, not exact wording.
I distinguished first responses, retries and self-review in my interpretation.
I recorded precise revision priorities rather than treating a raw score as mastery.
